results.verified_title: How research funding turned ideas into UK unicorns — EPSRC-supported spin-out portfolio
results.source_identity_basis: UK Research and Innovation original EPSRC impact article, explicitly published 23 September 2026; source identifies its portfolio metrics as of July 2026. Matched article title, institutional publisher, and date on the live primary page.
results.source_type: Official research-council impact assessment and spin-out portfolio report
results.evidence_location: UKRI/EPSRC article, introduction and portfolio metrics paragraph beginning As of July 2026; independent HESA official spin-out register context and methodology.
results.specific_finding: EPSRC reports at least 1,900 direct spin-outs arising from its research base, of which 1,041 remained active as of July 2026. UKRI attributes at least £14 billion collective value, over £8 billion annual turnover, more than 30,700 jobs, and over £9 billion raised investment to the portfolio; these are council-attributed portfolio totals rather than independently audited causal impacts.
results.primary_evidence_summary: EPSRC published quantitative results for direct research spin-outs, survival and portfolio scale in September 2026. HESA separately publishes national university spin-out records and methodological definitions, showing measurable national research commercialisation but not independently validating the EPSRC-attributed 1,900-company total.
results.corroboration_assessment: Independent HESA administrative register and University of Cambridge research report establish substantial UK university spin-out activity and caution on populations and definition changes. They corroborate the research-commercialisation mechanism, not the exact EPSRC-attributed portfolio figures or its causal impact.
results.mechanism_and_ri_importance: Research council investment can support the commercialisation pipeline through university IP-based companies, staff and fellow training, translational grants, and later investment. The reported stock of surviving companies provides a scale indicator for the UK innovation ecosystem.
results.eu_radar_comparison: Not found as this dated EPSRC portfolio source in the inspected Global Deep Scan 24-case submission or the repository snapshot’s Global verified-findings archive. This is a snapshot-level coverage comparison, not a claim about the live main Radar.
results.method_and_limitations: Attribution to EPSRC-supported research is not experimental causation; portfolio definitions may overlap broader UK spin-out registers and may vary over time. UKRI reporting and HESA counts measure different populations and cannot be subtracted or interpreted as consistent time-series observations. Financial values are UKRI-reported, not independently re-audited here.

results.verified_title: HESA UK university spin-out register: 2026 updated company counts and methodological corrections
results.source_identity_basis: Higher Education Statistics Agency official spin-out register release notes, with explicit 12 June and 18 June 2026 corrections and April 2026 original publication. Verified primary page reports 2,560 unique companies and 147 founded in academic year 2024/25.
results.source_type: Official UK higher-education administrative statistics in development, with release corrections
results.evidence_location: HESA Spin-out register, Total number of spin-out companies, Update 12th June 2026, and Update 18th June 2026 sections; Cambridge Policy Evidence Unit repository report for independent analytic context.
results.specific_finding: The corrected 2026 HESA university spin-out register includes 2,560 unique spin-out firms, excluding 31 commercially sensitive stealth-mode companies, and records 147 unique spin-outs founded in 2024/25, excluding 12 stealth-mode firms. June 2026 corrections added 25 omitted firms, removed one ineligible firm, and revised a 2024/25 count from 140 to 147.
results.primary_evidence_summary: The HESA release is an actual administrative dataset update with named correction types and defined reference period, rather than an undated service description. The counts cover firms originating from UK higher-education providers, with special rules on founding dates, activity status and historical coverage.
results.corroboration_assessment: Cambridge university research and Research England analysis independently establish the dataset infrastructure and importance of careful definitional and cohort comparisons. Their earlier 2025 register count of 2,307 is not directly equivalent to the corrected HESA 2026 population and should not be treated as simple organic growth.
results.mechanism_and_ri_importance: A nationally curated spin-out register expands observability of knowledge transfer from research organisations into companies; reproducible firm-level counts and correction histories can support sector, location and investor-network analyses of innovation-system activity.
results.eu_radar_comparison: The exact June 2026 corrected HESA administrative register was absent from the previously imported 24 cases and not found in the repository snapshot’s Global verified-findings archive. No assertion is made that the live main Radar lacks all coverage of UK spin-outs.
results.method_and_limitations: Official statistics are in development and include retrospective provider updates, stealth-company suppression and coverage choices; an administrative increase cannot by itself demonstrate new-firm formation or a productivity improvement. The dataset extends through the 2024/25 academic year, not a full 2026 firm-creation cohort.
